blocks.label: Core message
blocks.text: North America is the largest region (41.27% of global revenue) and one market in size but three in route to market: an FDA-led U.S., an operator-led Canada and a tender-led Mexico.

blocks.note: Demand rests on high transfusion volumes and automation.
blocks.text: The region is supported by established blood-center networks, high transfusion activity and broad adoption of automated immunohematology and donor screening. Revenue reaches **USD 2,360.70 Mn** by 2033.

blocks.label: Consultant implication
blocks.text: Win the U.S. on automation, connectivity and clearance speed; qualify with Canadian blood operators; and reach Mexico through distributors able to handle tenders and CNTS evaluation.

items.title: U.S.: scale and automation
items.text: Leads adoption of automated immunohematology, gel and column systems, donor-screening immunoassays and connected blood-bank software.

items.title: Canada: centralized operators
items.text: Canadian Blood Services and Héma-Québec; extended antigen matching and reference immunohematology services.

items.title: Mexico: tenders and distributors
items.text: Institutional tenders and distributor-supported laboratory channels; COFEPRIS registration and CNTS oversight.

blocks.text: Suppliers compete through portfolio breadth, platform placement, reagent pull-through, service contracts, technical support and workflow connectivity.

strengths: High U.S. collection volumes (~11 Mn whole-blood units a year)
weaknesses: Fragmented procurement in Canada and Mexico
Validation and interoperability burden when switching platforms
opportunities: Canadian reference testing and antigen matching
threats: Rising rivalry on automation and menu breadth

items.title: Phase 1: U.S. placements
items.text: Secure FDA clearances and win analyzer placements with LIS connectivity in hospital transfusion labs and blood centers.

items.title: Phase 2: Canadian qualification
items.text: Obtain Health Canada licensing and validate with Canadian Blood Services, Héma-Québec and provincial networks.

items.title: Phase 3: Mexican partners
items.text: Register with COFEPRIS, pass CNTS evaluation and enter tenders through distributors with service reach.
The U.S. adds USD 795.0 Mn of the region's USD 986.6 Mn increment (2025–2033).
Validation, training and antibody-history continuity protect incumbents.
Canada and Mexico buy through budgets and tenders, creating pricing discipline.
